The plan committed to Option D — a generic `App<R: Renderer>` struct in `lattice-host` parametrised over a host-side `Renderer` trait with two associated types. This doc records the architectural problem that surfaced *during* the 5.B.3 attempt to move the struct, and the pivot to Option E (composition) that resolved it.\\n\\n## What broke Option D\\n\\nRust's orphan rule: **inherent `impl` blocks must live in the crate that defines the implementing type.** Once `App` moves to `lattice-host`, every `impl App<TuiRenderer>` in `lattice-ui-tui` is forbidden, because `App` is foreign to `lattice-ui-tui`. The `<TuiRenderer>` specialisation doesn't help — the implementing *type* is `App`, and that's what the orphan rule checks.\\n\\nThat breaks the plan in [`phase-5b-app-fields.md`](phase-5b-app-fields.md) \\\"Open question 2\\\": the answer there — \\\"leave [TUI-specific methods] in lattice-ui-tui as `impl App` (where `App = host::App<TuiRenderer>`)\\\" — is not legal Rust. The type alias does not change the orphan-rule answer.\\n\\nThe reachable workarounds inside Option D are:\\n\\n1.\\t**Mega-commit**: move `App` and *every* `impl App` block across ~25 files in `lattice-ui-tui/src/app/*.rs` in a single commit (~35k LoC of code motion). Within that commit, each block becomes `impl<R: Renderer> App<R>`, and the handful of methods that touch `theme` / `pane_render_registry` concretely either (a) move to `impl App<TuiRenderer>` *in lattice-host*, which is legal but forces lattice-host to know about `TuiRenderer` (a layering violation — host must not depend on its renderer), or (b) get rewritten as extension-trait impls in lattice-ui-tui.\\n2.\\t**Extension-trait pattern**: same as (1)(b), used everywhere a TUI-specific method exists. Every call site needs `use TuiAppExt;` (or one of several traits, depending on how we slice). Lots of imports, especially across tests.\\n\\nNeither is awful, but neither is graceful. (1) sacrifices the \\\"every commit green\\\" discipline that has held throughout the Phase 5 migration. (2) imposes lifelong ergonomic cost on call sites for a small number of TUI methods.\\n\\n## What Option F (`trait App`) would look like\\n\\nA trait can mean two distinct things in this context:\\n\\n- **Pure interface trait + duplicated state.** Each renderer's app struct holds its own copy of the ~198 renderer-agnostic fields, and the trait declares the common behaviour. The compiler enforces the contract, but the data duplicates between renderers. As the editor evolves, the two App structs drift unless we paper over it with macros, which restore the old problem in a different form.\\n- **Interface trait + shared state struct.** A `trait Editor` declares methods; concrete impl structs hold an `EditorCore` for shared state plus their renderer-specific fields. This is *Option E with an extra trait layer*. The trait only earns its keep if some host-level code needs to be generic over \\\"any renderer's editor\\\" — but nothing in the codebase has that shape. Host-level code takes `&mut EditorCore` directly.\\n\\nIn both readings, the trait doesn't pay for itself. Option F is not chosen.\\n\\n## Option E: composition\\n\\n```rust\\n// lattice-host:\\npub struct Editor {\\n\\tpub cursor: Position,\\n\\tpub mode: ModalState,\\n\\tpub buffer_registry: BufferRegistry,\\n\\t// ... ~198 renderer-agnostic fields, taken from the audit's HOST clusters\\n}\\n\\nimpl Editor {\\n\\tpub fn dispatch(&mut self, action: Action) { ... }\\n\\tpub fn set_message(&mut self, msg: EchoMessage) { ... }\\n\\t// ... ~99% of today's `impl App` methods\\n}\\n\\n// lattice-ui-tui:\\npub struct App {\\n\\tpub editor: Editor,\\n\\tpub theme: TuiTheme,\\n\\tpub pane_render_registry: TuiPaneRenderRegistry,\\n}\\n\\nimpl App {\\n\\tpub fn new(...) -> Self { ... }\\n\\tpub fn sync_theme_from_config(&mut self) { ... }\\n\\t// ... small set of methods that touch theme / pane_render_registry\\n}\\n```\\n\\n`Editor` is the renderer-agnostic editor state. `App` is a thin renderer-specific wrapper composing `Editor` with the renderer's caches. GPUI's analogue:\\n\\n```rust\\n// future lattice-ui-gpui:\\npub struct App {\\n\\tpub editor: Editor,\\n\\tpub theme: GpuiTheme,\\n\\tpub pane_render_registry: GpuiPaneRenderRegistry,\\n}\\n```\\n\\nSame `Editor`, different wrapper. No code duplication; no generics; no orphan rule.\\n\\n### Evaluation against the paramount goals\\n\\n1.\\t**Performance.** Direct field access through `self.editor.foo` is zero-cost — the compiler flattens the access pattern to a single pointer add. Identical to Option D's monomorphised generics. No virtual dispatch.\\n\\n2.\\t**Extensibility.** Adding a renderer = \\\"define an App struct composing `Editor` + your renderer-specific fields, implement the rendering crate's trait.\\\" No constraints on the renderer's App shape beyond holding an `Editor`. Plugin host code (Phase 6+) talks to `Editor` directly — never to the renderer wrapper.\\n\\n3.\\t**Vim modal editing.** Unaffected; the modal engine and grammar live on `Editor`.\\n\\n4.\\t**Asynchronicity.** Unaffected; async actors hold `&mut Editor` (renderer-agnostic) or are owned by it as today.\\n\\n### Evaluation against the design heuristics\\n\\n1.\\t*Best long-term fit beats easy implementation.* Option D is \\\"fancier\\\" in type-system terms; Option E is more boring Rust. Both are zero-cost. The orphan rule is a structural feature of the language — fighting it with extension traits is paying ongoing tax for a one-time architectural choice. Composition is the long-term-fit answer.\\n\\n2.\\t*Evaluate against paramount goals, not other editors.* Both options serve the goals equivalently. The deciding factor is structural cleanliness, not feature parity.\\n\\n3.\\t*Treat user-suggested options as input, not the menu.* The user proposed F (trait); the answer is E (composition), with the reasoning above.\\n\\n4.\\t*Confirm the plan before non-trivial work.* This doc is that confirmation. Code change waits.\\n\\n5.\\t*Non-trivial design changes ship four artefacts together.* For 5.B.3 onwards: docs (this file + ledger updates), tests (existing test suite covers; per-cluster commits keep coverage), benches (no perf impact — composition is zero-cost — so no new bench targets), error handling (unchanged from today). \\n\\n### What composition costs\\n\\n- **Field access prefix.** Code that today writes `app.cursor = pos` becomes `app.editor.cursor = pos`. Inside `impl Editor` methods (which is where most of today's `impl App` methods migrate to), it's still `self.cursor = pos` — no prefix needed. The prefix appears only at the *outer boundary*: where the TUI runtime calls into editor state from outside an `impl Editor` method. The audit notes those call sites are bounded to `render.rs`, `runtime.rs`, the keymap catalog dispatchers, and a few `impl App` methods that genuinely need both `editor` and `theme` in scope.\\n- **Two struct names.** `Editor` (state) vs `App` (renderer wrapper). The naming is honest: `Editor` is the editor; `App` is the renderer-specific composed thing.\\n- **No `Deref` impl.** Resisting the temptation to add `impl Deref<Target = Editor> for App` keeps method resolution unambiguous. Worth the small ergonomic cost.\\n\\n## Migration plan\\n\\nThe migration is intrinsically per-cluster: each commit moves a coherent slice of fields from `App` to `Editor`, plus the methods that touch only those fields. Methods that touch fields not yet migrated stay on `App` and use `self.editor.foo` for the migrated subset.\\n\\nField clusters from the audit, ordered by migration friendliness:\\n\\n1.\\t**Document + active-pane state** (cursor, scroll, document, buffers, pane_tree, viewport, ...).\\n2.\\t**Modal + dispatch** (modal, partial_chord, registry, builtins, action_ids, keymap, ...).\\n3.\\t**Cmdline + echo** (command_line, last_message, messages, command_history, ...).\\n4.\\t**Syntax** (lang_registry, syntax, pending_syntax_edits, visible_highlights, ...).\\n5.\\t**Search + vim state** (search_line, last_search, marks, registers, position_history, ...).\\n6.\\t**Config + modes** (config, option_cache, mode_registry, services, ...).\\n7.\\t**Popup + help** (popup_buffer, popup_back_stack, prev_pane_for_help, ...).\\n8.\\t**Completion** (completion_registry, completion_state, insert_completion, snippets, ...).\\n9.\\t**Picker** (picker, picker_registry, picker_mru, ...).\\n10.\\t**LSP request channels** (~40 pending_*_rx/_token fields).\\n11.\\t**LSP per-buffer caches** (~12 lsp_*_cache fields).\\n12.\\t**LSP subsystem handles + watchers** (lsp, lsp_file_watcher, lsp_diagnostics, ...).\\n\\nEach cluster gets its own commit. Method moves accompany field moves: methods that only touch migrated fields move to `impl Editor` in lattice-host; methods that touch both migrated and unmigrated fields stay on `impl App` and access migrated fields via `self.editor`.\\n\\nHalfway through, App looks like:\\n\\n```rust\\npub struct App {\\n\\tpub editor: Editor,           // grows over migration\\n\\tpub theme: TuiTheme,\\n\\tpub pane_render_registry: TuiPaneRenderRegistry,\\n\\t// fields that haven't migrated yet, shrinking\\n}\\n```\\n\\nThe endpoint: `App` holds `editor` + `theme` + `pane_render_registry` only. Every other field has migrated to `Editor`. `impl App`'s surface is small and TUI-specific.\\n\\n### What ships before the per-cluster work begins\\n\\n**5.B.3 (revised — small commit, ships green, no semantic change):**\\n\\n1.\\tRevert the 5.B.2 `App<R: Renderer>` parametrisation: change `pub struct App<R: lattice_host::Renderer = crate::TuiRenderer>` back to `pub struct App`. Restore `theme: crate::theme::Theme` and `pane_render_registry: crate::pane_render::PaneRenderRegistry` to concrete types.\\n2.\\tDefine `lattice_host::editor::Editor` as an empty pub struct (the destination for the migration).\\n3.\\tAdd `pub editor: lattice_host::editor::Editor` field to `App`. Initialise to `Editor::default()` (derive `Default`).\\n4.\\tDecide on the fate of `lattice_host::Renderer` + `TuiRenderer` + `MinimalRenderer`. **Recommendation: keep them.** They became unused-by-`App` but are still potentially useful for Phase 5.6's `lattice-render::Renderer` trait, where they may legitimately appear as marker bounds or trait-object segregators. Keeping them is harmless; if Phase 5.6 doesn't end up needing them, we delete then.\\n\\nAfter 5.B.3, all subsequent commits are field-cluster migrations (5.B.4, 5.B.5, …) until App's surface is reduced to the renderer-specific shape.\\n\\n### Why composition unblocks the \\\"every commit green\\\" discipline\\n\\nUnder Option D's mega-commit, intermediate states are not buildable: `impl App` blocks in unmoved files can't see the new `App<R>` signature; `impl<R: Renderer> App<R>` blocks in moved files can't be referenced from unmoved code that still says `App`. The only legal landing is \\\"everything at once.\\\"\\n\\nUnder Option E, intermediate states *are* buildable:\\n- A field moved from `App` to `Editor` is accessed via `self.editor.foo` at the call site (whether that call site is in `impl App` or anywhere else).\\n- A method moved from `impl App` to `impl Editor` is callable as `app.editor.foo(...)` from callers; if the caller is itself in `impl Editor`, it's just `self.foo(...)`.\\n- The host-side methods on `Editor` work directly; the renderer-side wrapper code that needs both `editor` and `theme` borrows them separately at the same scope.\\n\\nEach commit can:\\n- Move N fields from `App` to `Editor`,\\n- Move M methods from `impl App` to `impl Editor` (where the method's body references no unmoved fields and no renderer-specific fields),\\n- Rewrite call sites for the moved fields from `self.foo` → `self.editor.foo` *within* methods that stay on `impl App` and still need those fields,\\n- Leave everything else untouched,\\n\\nand the workspace continues to build and test.\\n\\nThis is the property that broke Option D and that Option E restores.\\n\\n## Decision\\n\\nPivot from Option D to Option E. Restart 5.B.3 with the smaller scope above. The remaining slices (5.B.4 onward) become per-cluster migrations. The end state is the same one the audit anticipated — host owns the editor's logic; renderer owns its rendering — but reached through composition rather than generic parametrisation.\\n\",\"numLines\":168,\"startLine\":1,\"totalLines\":168}}"</outcome>

The `*messages*` buffer's per-tick drain\\n    ///    ([`Self::drain_message_events`]) appends each record.\\n    ///\\n    /// **msg-mode.1 contract:** `set_message` writes directly\\n    /// to the ring + bus (the legacy path). The\\n    /// [`lattice_runtime::MessagesLayer`] installed at boot\\n    /// captures every *other* `tracing::*` event in the editor\\n    /// (LSP layer logs, plugin host, future telemetry) into\\n    /// the same ring + bus. Keeping\\n    /// `set_message` independent of the global subscriber\\n    /// preserves per-App isolation — each App's bus + ring are\\n    /// the only consumers of its own `set_message` calls.\\n    pub fn set_message(&mut self, level: EchoLevel, text: impl Into<String>) {\\n        let text: String = text.into();\\n        self.editor.last_message = Some(EchoMessage {\\n            text: text.clone(),\\n            level,\\n        });\\n        let record = MessageRecord {\\n            timestamp: std::time::SystemTime::now(),\\n            level: echo_level_to_wire(level),\\n            text,\\n        };\\n        if let Ok(mut ring) = self.editor.messages.lock() {\\n            ring.push(record.clone());\\n        }\\n        self.editor.event_bus.publish_typed(MessagePushed { record });\\n    }\\n}\\n\\npub(crate) fn line_byte_len(buf: &Buffer, line: u32) -> u32 {\\n    // §8.2 hot path: use ropey's O(log n) line API instead of\\n    // materialising the whole buffer.\\n    buf.line_byte_len(line)\\n}\\n\\npub(crate) fn last_addressable_line(buf: &Buffer) -> u32 {\\n    let lc = buf.line_count();\\n    if lc == 0 {\\n        return 0;\\n    }\\n    // ropey reports an extra empty line for any rope ending in\\n    // `\\\\n`. Detect that by checking whether the last \\\"line\\\" the\\n    // rope reports is empty, without materialising the entire\\n    // buffer text.\\n    let last_idx = lc - 1;\\n    if buf.line_byte_len(last_idx) == 0 && lc >= 2 {\\n        last_idx - 1\\n    } else {\\n        last_idx\\n    }\\n}\\n\\npub(super) fn is_valid_mark_name(c: char) -> bool {\\n    c.is_ascii_alphabetic() || c.is_ascii_digit()\\n}\\n\\n/// Render a register's content into a one-line preview (truncated and\\n/// with newlines escaped). Used by `:reg`.\\npub(super) fn preview_register(s: &str) -> String {\\n    const MAX: usize = 40;\\n    let escaped: String = s\\n        .chars()\\n        .map(|c| if c == '\\\\n' { '\\\\u{21B5}' } else { c })\\n        .collect();\\n    if escaped.chars().count() <= MAX {\\n        escaped\\n    } else {\\n        let trimmed: String = escaped.chars().take(MAX).collect();\\n        format!(\\\"{trimmed}…\\\")\\n    }\\n}\\n\\npub(super) fn is_word_char_byte(b: u8) -> bool {\\n    b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b == b'_'\\n}\\n\\n/// Cross-source visual dedup for the insert-completion popup\\n/// (Phase 4.2.g.7 polish). Keeps the FIRST occurrence of each\\n/// `raw.text`; subsequent rows with the same text drop out.\\n/// Called after the ranker has sorted descending by score, so\\n/// the surviving row is the highest-ranked entry per text --\\n/// the buffer-words copy of `outer` outranks the tree-sitter\\n/// copy at the spec's 100/80 priority split, so the popup row\\n/// for `outer` carries the buffer-words tag.\\n///\\n/// Selection / navigation / accept all index into the deduped\\n/// vec naturally; this is the only place we coalesce rows\\n/// across sources, and it runs before the popup paints.\\npub(super) fn dedup_rendered_by_text(rendered: &mut Vec<lattice_completion::RenderedCandidate>) {\\n    let mut seen: std::collections::HashSet<String> = std::collections::HashSet::new();\\n    rendered.retain(|cand| seen.insert(cand.raw.text.clone()));\\n}\\n\\n/// True for bytes the path-completion source treats as part of\\n/// a filename / directory component. Wider than `is_word_char_byte`\\n/// so common filename characters (`.`, `-`, `~`) ride the same\\n/// segment; the trigger anchor breaks at `/` (dir boundary)\\n/// rather than at these characters.\\npub(super) fn is_path_byte(b: u8) -> bool {\\n    b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(b, b'_' | b'-' | b'.' | b'~' | b'+' | b'@')\\n}\\n\\n/// Expand `~/...` against `$HOME` and absolutise a relative\\n/// path against the process's current working directory.\\n///\\n/// Two failure modes this closes:\\n///\\n/// 1. `:e ~/foo.rs` -- without expansion, `Document::open`\\n///    forwards the literal `~` to `read_to_string` and fails\\n///    ENOENT. Cwd-failure or HOME-missing falls\\n/// through to the input verbatim; the caller's open then\\n/// produces the same error it would have produced without\\n/// the normalise step.\\npub(super) fn normalize_user_path(path: &std::path::Path) -> std::path::PathBuf {\\n    let expanded = expand_tilde(path);\\n    if expanded.is_absolute() {\\n        return expanded;\\n    }\\n    match std::env::current_dir() {\\n        Ok(cwd) => cwd.join(expanded),\\n        Err(_) => expanded,\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n/// `~/rest` → `$HOME/rest`, `~` alone → `$HOME`. Mirrors the helper in\\n/// `lattice-completion::builtins::generators` -- they stay\\n/// in lockstep because the cmdline-completion source and the\\n/// `:e` submit path both flow through user-typed strings.\\nfn expand_tilde(path: &std::path::Path) -> std::path::PathBuf {\\n    let Some(s) = path.to_str() else {\\n        return path.to_path_buf();\\n    };\\n    let Some(home) = std::env::var_os(\\\"HOME\\\") else {\\n        return path.to_path_buf();\\n    };\\n    if s == \\\"~\\\" {\\n        return std::path::PathBuf::from(home);\\n    }\\n    if let Some(rest) = s.strip_prefix(\\\"~/\\\") {\\n        return std::path::PathBuf::from(home).join(rest);\\n    }\\n    path.to_path_buf()\\n}\\n\\n/// True if `line_idx` is empty or whitespace-only. Used by the\\n/// fold-aware j/k snap to swallow trailing blanks between sibling\\n/// folds (so `j` from a closed fold's heading lands on the next\\n/// sibling's heading, not on the blank between them).\\npub(super) fn is_blank_line(buffer: &lattice_core::Buffer, line_idx: u32) -> bool {\\n    buffer\\n        .line(line_idx)\\n        .map(|s| s.trim().is_empty())\\n        .unwrap_or(true)\\n}\\n\\n/// Phase 4.2 features (hover, definition, references, completion)\\n/// all need this; later we'll thread the per-server negotiated\\n/// `PositionEncodingKind` through here so utf-8 / utf-32 servers\\n/// don't pay the utf-16 conversion. For 4.2.b utf-16 is correct\\n/// for every server we care about today.\\n/// Render an LSP `SignatureHelp` response into a markdown body\\n/// the popup renderer can display. Picks the active signature\\n/// (server-supplied `active_signature` index, default 0) and\\n/// inlines the active parameter's documentation when present.\\n/// Returns the empty string when the response carries no\\n/// signatures.\\npub(crate) fn signature_help_to_markdown(sh: &lsp_types::SignatureHelp) -> String {\\n    if sh.signatures.is_empty() {\\n        return String::new();\\n    }\\n    let active_sig_idx = sh.active_signature.unwrap_or(0) as usize;\\n    let sig = sh\\n        .signatures\\n        .get(active_sig_idx)\\n        .or_else(|| sh.signatures.first())\\n        .expect(\\\"non-empty checked above\\\");\\n    let mut out = String::new();\\n    // Active signature's call form -- renders as a fenced code\\n    // block so the popup's markdown highlighter picks up\\n    // syntax highlighting (whatever language the server says\\n    // -- we don't know, so default to text).\\n    out.push_str(\\\"```text\\\\n\\\");\\n    out.push_str(&sig.label);\\n    out.push_str(\\\"\\\\n```\\\\n\\\");\\n    // Parameter highlight: append a short note pointing at the\\n    // active parameter's name. The popup overlay doesn't yet\\n    // do per-character paragraph styling, so this is the\\n    // friendliest representation we have without bespoke\\n    // rendering.\\n    if let Some(active_param_idx) = sig.active_parameter.or(sh.active_parameter)\\n        && let Some(params) = sig.parameters.as_ref()\\n        && let Some(param) = params.get(active_param_idx as usize)\\n    {\\n        let label_str = match &param.label {\\n            lsp_types::ParameterLabel::Simple(s) => s.clone(),\\n            lsp_types::ParameterLabel::LabelOffsets(_) => String::new(),\\n        };\\n        if !label_str.is_empty() {\\n            out.push_str(&format!(\\\"\\\\n**param:** `{label_str}`\\\\n\\\"));\\n        }\\n        if let Some(doc) = param.documentation.as_ref() {\\n            let doc_str = match doc {\\n                lsp_types::Documentation::String(s) => s.clone(),\\n                lsp_types::Documentation::MarkupContent(mc) => mc.value.clone(),\\n            };\\n            if !doc_str.is_empty() {\\n                out.push('\\\\n');\\n                out.push_str(&doc_str);\\n                out.push('\\\\n');\\n            }\\n        }\\n    }\\n    // Signature-level documentation when present.\\n    if let Some(doc) = sig.documentation.as_ref() {\\n        let doc_str = match doc {\\n            lsp_types::Documentation::String(s) => s.clone(),\\n            lsp_types::Documentation::MarkupContent(mc) => mc.value.clone(),\\n        };\\n        if !doc_str.is_empty() {\\n            out.push('\\\\n');\\n            out.push_str(&doc_str);\\n            out.push('\\\\n');\\n        }\\n    }\\n    out\\n}\\n\\n/// Inverse of `app_to_lsp_position` -- LSP utf-16 character\\n/// column → utf-8 byte column on the given line. Used by\\n/// `apply_lsp_text_edits` to convert TextEdit ranges back to\\n/// the App's `Position` shape.\\npub(crate) fn lsp_position_to_app_byte(buffer: &Buffer, line: u32, character: u32) -> u32 {\\n    let line_text = buffer.line(line).unwrap_or_default();\\n    lattice_lsp::position::utf16_column_to_utf8_byte(&line_text, character)\\n}\\n\\n/// 4.4.e: does the App `(line, byte)` cursor sit inside the\\n/// half-open LSP `range`? We compare only by (line, character)\\n/// in LSP utf-16 space because the range itself is LSP-shape;\\n/// the App cursor is converted on the fly.\\npub(crate) fn cursor_inside_range(cursor: Position, range: &lsp_types::Range) -> bool {\\n    let line = cursor.line;\\n    let col = cursor.byte;\\n    let start = (range.start.line, range.start.character);\\n    let end = (range.end.line, range.end.character);\\n    let here = (line, col);\\n    here >= start && here < end\\n}\\n\\n/// 4.4.f: convert an LSP `FoldingRange` to our `Fold`. LSP\\n/// returns line-based extents; the identity hash combines\\n/// start_line + end_line + kind so closed-state survives\\n/// re-fetches that produce the same logical fold.\\npub(crate) fn folding_range_to_fold(r: lsp_types::FoldingRange) -> Fold {\\n    use std::hash::{Hash, Hasher};\\n    let mut hasher = std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher::new();\\n    r.start_line.hash(&mut hasher);\\n    r.end_line.hash(&mut hasher);\\n    // Spec omits a stable u32 for `kind`; hash the string form\\n    // when present so a fold's kind change still re-keys.\\n    if let Some(kind) = r.kind.as_ref() {\\n        std::mem::discriminant(kind).hash(&mut hasher);\\n    }\\n    Fold {\\n        start_line: r.start_line,\\n        end_line: r.end_line,\\n        closed: false,\\n        identity: Some(hasher.finish()),\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n/// 4.4.e: flatten an LSP `SelectionRange` (linked list via\\n/// `parent`) into a `Vec<Range>` ordered innermost-first.\\npub(crate) fn flatten_selection_range_chain(\\n    head: &lsp_types::SelectionRange,\\n) -> Vec<lsp_types::Range> {\\n    let mut out = Vec::new();\\n    let mut cur = Some(head);\\n    while let Some(node) = cur {\\n        out.push(node.range);\\n        cur = node.parent.as_deref();\\n    }\\n    out\\n}\\n\\npub(crate) fn app_to_lsp_position(buffer: &Buffer, p: Position) -> Option<lsp_types::Position> {\\n    let line_text = buffer.line(p.line)?;\\n    let character = lattice_lsp::position::utf8_byte_to_utf16_column(&line_text, p.byte);\\n    Some(lsp_types::Position {\\n        line: p.line,\\n        character,\\n    })\\n}\\n\\n/// Flatten a `DocumentSymbolResponse` into our pre-rendered\\n/// `SymbolRow` shape. The legacy `Flat(Vec<SymbolInformation>)`\\n/// variant is one row per symbol with no nesting; the modern\\n/// `Nested(Vec<DocumentSymbol>)` variant carries\\n/// `children: Vec<DocumentSymbol>`, walked depth-first to\\n/// preserve outline ordering.\\npub(crate) fn flatten_document_symbol_response(\\n    resp: lsp_types::DocumentSymbolResponse,\\n    path: &std::path::Path,\\n    out: &mut Vec<SymbolRow>,\\n) {\\n    match resp {\\n        lsp_types::DocumentSymbolResponse::Flat(syms) => {\\n            for sym in syms {\\n                if let Some(row) = symbol_information_to_row(&sym) {\\n                    out.push(row);\\n                }\\n            }\\n        }\\n        lsp_types::DocumentSymbolResponse::Nested(syms) => {\\n            fn walk(\\n                syms: Vec<lsp_types::DocumentSymbol>,\\n                path: &std::path::Path,\\n                depth: u32,\\n                out: &mut Vec<SymbolRow>,\\n            ) {\\n                for sym in syms {\\n                    out.push(SymbolRow {\\n                        name: sym.name.clone(),\\n                        kind_glyph: symbol_kind_glyph(sym.kind),\\n                        container: None,\\n                        depth,\\n                        path: path.to_path_buf(),\\n                        line: sym.selection_range.start.line,\\n                        col: sym.selection_range.start.character,\\n                    });\\n                    if let Some(children) = sym.children {\\n                        walk(children, path, depth + 1, out);\\n                    }\\n                }\\n            }\\n            walk(syms, path, 0, out);\\n        }\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n/// Map a flat `SymbolInformation` (legacy outline + workspace\\n/// symbol shape) into our row type. Returns `None` when the\\n/// location's URI doesn't resolve to a path.\\n/// Convert a modern (LSP 3.17+) `WorkspaceSymbol` into a\\n/// `SymbolRow` (Phase 4.2 follow-up). Returns `None` when:\\n/// - The URI doesn't map to a path.\\n/// - Resolve fails (server doesn't actually advertise it,\\n///   or returns a still-unresolved shape).\\n/// - Cancellation fires while we're awaiting resolve.\\npub(crate) async fn workspace_symbol_to_row(\\n    handle: &lattice_lsp::ServerHandle,\\n    sym: lsp_types::WorkspaceSymbol,\\n    token: &lattice_protocol::CancellationToken,\\n) -> Option<SymbolRow> {\\n    use lsp_types::OneOf;\\n    let (path, line, col) = match &sym.location {\\n        OneOf::Left(loc) => (\\n            lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&loc.uri)?,\\n            loc.range.start.line,\\n            loc.range.start.character,\\n        ),\\n        OneOf::Right(wsl) => {\\n            let path = lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&wsl.uri)?;\\n            // Server's resolveProvider absent -> no point firing.\\n            // Fall back to (0, 0); the user can still navigate\\n            // to the file.\\n            if !handle.capabilities().workspace_symbol_resolve_provider() {\\n                (path, 0, 0)\\n            } else {\\n                match handle\\n                    .workspace_symbol_resolve(sym.clone(), token.clone())\\n                    .await\\n                {\\n                    Ok(resolved) => match resolved.location {\\n                        OneOf::Left(loc) => (\\n                            lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&loc.uri).unwrap_or(path),\\n                            loc.range.start.line,\\n                            loc.range.start.character,\\n                        ),\\n                        // Server replied without populating range\\n                        // -- spec violation, but defensive: fall\\n                        // back to (0, 0) instead of dropping.\\n                        OneOf::Right(_) => (path, 0, 0),\\n                    },\\n                    // Resolve failed -- log via the symbol's\\n                    // path-only fallback. Caller still gets a\\n                    // navigable row.\\n                    Err(_) => (path, 0, 0),\\n                }\\n            }\\n        }\\n    };\\n    Some(SymbolRow {\\n        name: sym.name,\\n        kind_glyph: symbol_kind_glyph(sym.kind),\\n        container: sym.container_name,\\n        depth: 0,\\n        path,\\n        line,\\n        col,\\n    })\\n}\\n\\npub(crate) fn symbol_information_to_row(sym: &lsp_types::SymbolInformation) -> Option<SymbolRow> {\\n    let path = lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&sym.location.uri)?;\\n    Some(SymbolRow {\\n        name: sym.name.clone(),\\n        kind_glyph: symbol_kind_glyph(sym.kind),\\n        container: sym.container_name.clone(),\\n        depth: 0,\\n        path,\\n        line: sym.location.range.start.line,\\n        col: sym.location.range.start.character,\\n    })\\n}\\n\\n/// 4.5.a: render one `CallHierarchyItem` (the caller in an\\n/// `IncomingCall.from` or the callee in an\\n/// `OutgoingCall.to`) as a [`SymbolRow`] for the picker. The\\n/// item's `detail` (if any) plus the *originating* callable's\\n/// name ride in `container` -- e.g. for an incoming-calls\\n/// listing of `foo`, the rows say \\\"bar.rs:42 fn quux  (in foo)\\\".\\n/// Falls back to `(path, 0, 0)` if the URI doesn't parse;\\n/// keeping the row visible beats silently dropping it.\\npub(crate) fn call_hierarchy_to_row(\\n    item: &lsp_types::CallHierarchyItem,\\n    related_to: &str,\\n) -> SymbolRow {\\n    let path = lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&item.uri).unwrap_or_default();\\n    SymbolRow {\\n        name: item.name.clone(),\\n        kind_glyph: symbol_kind_glyph(item.kind),\\n        container: Some(format!(\\\"in {related_to}\\\")),\\n        depth: 0,\\n        path,\\n        line: item.selection_range.start.line,\\n        col: item.selection_range.start.character,\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n/// 4.5.c: does the given `range` cover the LSP `position`?\\n/// Inclusive on both ends (matches VSCode's \\\"click-through\\\"\\n/// semantics on a link's rightmost char). Cwd-failure or HOME-missing falls\\n/// through to the input verbatim; the caller's open then\\n/// produces the same error it would have produced without\\n/// the normalise step.\\npub(super) fn normalize_user_path(path: &std::path::Path) -> std::path::PathBuf {\\n    let expanded = expand_tilde(path);\\n    if expanded.is_absolute() {\\n        return expanded;\\n    }\\n    match std::env::current_dir() {\\n        Ok(cwd) => cwd.join(expanded),\\n        Err(_) => expanded,\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n/// `~/rest` → `$HOME/rest`, `~` alone → `$HOME`. LSP\\n/// returns line-based extents; the identity hash combines\\n/// start_line + end_line + kind so closed-state survives\\n/// re-fetches that produce the same logical fold.\\npub(crate) fn folding_range_to_fold(r: lsp_types::FoldingRange) -> Fold {\\n    use std::hash::{Hash, Hasher};\\n    let mut hasher = std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher::new();\\n    r.start_line.hash(&mut hasher);\\n    r.end_line.hash(&mut hasher);\\n    // Spec omits a stable u32 for `kind`; hash the string form\\n    // when present so a fold's kind change still re-keys.\\n    if let Some(kind) = r.kind.as_ref() {\\n        std::mem::discriminant(kind).hash(&mut hasher);\\n    }\\n    Fold {\\n        start_line: r.start_line,\\n        end_line: r.end_line,\\n        closed: false,\\n        identity: Some(hasher.finish()),\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n/// 4.4.e: flatten an LSP `SelectionRange` (linked list via\\n/// `parent`) into a `Vec<Range>` ordered innermost-first.\\npub(crate) fn flatten_selection_range_chain(\\n    head: &lsp_types::SelectionRange,\\n) -> Vec<lsp_types::Range> {\\n    let mut out = Vec::new();\\n    let mut cur = Some(head);\\n    while let Some(node) = cur {\\n        out.push(node.range);\\n        cur = node.parent.as_deref();\\n    }\\n    out\\n}\\n\\npub(crate) fn app_to_lsp_position(buffer: &Buffer, p: Position) -> Option<lsp_types::Position> {\\n    let line_text = buffer.line(p.line)?;\\n    let character = lattice_lsp::position::utf8_byte_to_utf16_column(&line_text, p.byte);\\n    Some(lsp_types::Position {\\n        line: p.line,\\n        character,\\n    })\\n}\\n\\n/// Flatten a `DocumentSymbolResponse` into our pre-rendered\\n/// `SymbolRow` shape. Returns `None` when:\\n/// - The URI doesn't map to a path.\\n/// - Resolve fails (server doesn't actually advertise it,\\n///   or returns a still-unresolved shape).\\n/// - Cancellation fires while we're awaiting resolve.\\npub(crate) async fn workspace_symbol_to_row(\\n    handle: &lattice_lsp::ServerHandle,\\n    sym: lsp_types::WorkspaceSymbol,\\n    token: &lattice_protocol::CancellationToken,\\n) -> Option<SymbolRow> {\\n    use lsp_types::OneOf;\\n    let (path, line, col) = match &sym.location {\\n        OneOf::Left(loc) => (\\n            lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&loc.uri)?,\\n            loc.range.start.line,\\n            loc.range.start.character,\\n        ),\\n        OneOf::Right(wsl) => {\\n            let path = lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&wsl.uri)?;\\n            // Server's resolveProvider absent -> no point firing.\\n            // Fall back to (0, 0); the user can still navigate\\n            // to the file.\\n            if !handle.capabilities().workspace_symbol_resolve_provider() {\\n                (path, 0, 0)\\n            } else {\\n                match handle\\n                    .workspace_symbol_resolve(sym.clone(), token.clone())\\n                    .await\\n                {\\n                    Ok(resolved) => match resolved.location {\\n                        OneOf::Left(loc) => (\\n                            lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&loc.uri).unwrap_or(path),\\n                            loc.range.start.line,\\n                            loc.range.start.character,\\n                        ),\\n                        // Server replied without populating range\\n                        // -- spec violation, but defensive: fall\\n                        // back to (0, 0) instead of dropping.\\n                        OneOf::Right(_) => (path, 0, 0),\\n                    },\\n                    // Resolve failed -- log via the symbol's\\n                    // path-only fallback. The `*messages*` buffer's per-tick drain\\n    ///    ([`Self::drain_message_events`]) appends each record.\\n    ///\\n    /// **msg-mode.1 contract:** `set_message` writes directly\\n    /// to the ring + bus (the legacy path). Returns `None` when:\\n/// - The URI doesn't map to a path.\\n/// - Resolve fails (server doesn't actually advertise it,\\n///   or returns a still-unresolved shape).\\n/// - Cancellation fires while we're awaiting resolve.\\npub(crate) async fn workspace_symbol_to_row(\\n    handle: &lattice_lsp::ServerHandle,\\n    sym: lsp_types::WorkspaceSymbol,\\n    token: &lattice_protocol::CancellationToken,\\n) -> Option<SymbolRow> {\\n    use lsp_types::OneOf;\\n    let (path, line, col) = match &sym.location {\\n        OneOf::Left(loc) => (\\n            lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&loc.uri)?,\\n            loc.range.start.line,\\n            loc.range.start.character,\\n        ),\\n        OneOf::Right(wsl) => {\\n            let path = lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&wsl.uri)?;\\n            // Server's resolveProvider absent -> no point firing.\\n            // Fall back to (0, 0); the user can still navigate\\n            // to the file.\\n            if !handle.capabilities().workspace_symbol_resolve_provider() {\\n                (path, 0, 0)\\n            } else {\\n                match handle\\n                    .workspace_symbol_resolve(sym.clone(), token.clone())\\n                    .await\\n                {\\n                    Ok(resolved) => match resolved.location {\\n                        OneOf::Left(loc) => (\\n                            lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&loc.uri).unwrap_or(path),\\n                            loc.range.start.line,\\n                            loc.range.start.character,\\n                        ),\\n                        // Server replied without populating range\\n                        // -- spec violation, but defensive: fall\\n                        // back to (0, 0) instead of dropping.\\n                        OneOf::Right(_) => (path, 0, 0),\\n                    },\\n                    // Resolve failed -- log via the symbol's\\n                    // path-only fallback. Two paths, one destination: every\\n    /// record the user sees in `*messages*` comes from one of\\n    /// these sources, and both produce identical\\n    /// `MessageRecord` shapes.\\n    ///\\n    /// **Why not route `set_message` through `tracing::event!`\\n    /// directly:** `tracing::subscriber::set_global_default` is\\n    /// process-wide. The first App installed captures the\\n    /// global subscriber; subsequent Apps (in tests, or\\n    /// multi-window setups) can't replace it. Keeping\\n    /// `set_message` independent of the global subscriber\\n    /// preserves per-App isolation — each App's bus + ring are\\n    /// the only consumers of its own `set_message` calls.\\n    pub fn set_message(&mut self, level: EchoLevel, text: impl Into<String>) {\\n        let text: String = text.into();\\n        self.editor.last_message = Some(EchoMessage {\\n            text: text.clone(),\\n            level,\\n        });\\n        let record = MessageRecord {\\n            timestamp: std::time::SystemTime::now(),\\n            level: echo_level_to_wire(level),\\n            text,\\n        };\\n        if let Ok(mut ring) = self.editor.messages.lock() {\\n            ring.push(record.clone());\\n        }\\n        self.editor.event_bus.publish_typed(MessagePushed { record });\\n    }\\n}\\n\\npub(crate) fn line_byte_len(buf: &Buffer, line: u32) -> u32 {\\n    // §8.2 hot path: use ropey's O(log n) line API instead of\\n    // materialising the whole buffer.\\n    buf.line_byte_len(line)\\n}\\n\\npub(crate) fn last_addressable_line(buf: &Buffer) -> u32 {\\n    let lc = buf.line_count();\\n    if lc == 0 {\\n        return 0;\\n    }\\n    // ropey reports an extra empty line for any rope ending in\\n    // `\\\\n`. Detect that by checking whether the last \\\"line\\\" the\\n    // rope reports is empty, without materialising the entire\\n    // buffer text.\\n    let last_idx = lc - 1;\\n    if buf.line_byte_len(last_idx) == 0 && lc >= 2 {\\n        last_idx - 1\\n    } else {\\n        last_idx\\n    }\\n}\\n\\npub(super) fn is_valid_mark_name(c: char) -> bool {\\n    c.is_ascii_alphabetic() || c.is_ascii_digit()\\n}\\n\\n/// Render a register's content into a one-line preview (truncated and\\n/// with newlines escaped). Used by `:reg`.\\npub(super) fn preview_register(s: &str) -> String {\\n    const MAX: usize = 40;\\n    let escaped: String = s\\n        .chars()\\n        .map(|c| if c == '\\\\n' { '\\\\u{21B5}' } else { c })\\n        .collect();\\n    if escaped.chars().count() <= MAX {\\n        escaped\\n    } else {\\n        let trimmed: String = escaped.chars().take(MAX).collect();\\n        format!(\\\"{trimmed}…\\\")\\n    }\\n}\\n\\npub(super) fn is_word_char_byte(b: u8) -> bool {\\n    b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b == b'_'\\n}\\n\\n/// Cross-source visual dedup for the insert-completion popup\\n/// (Phase 4.2.g.7 polish). Keeps the FIRST occurrence of each\\n/// `raw.text`; subsequent rows with the same text drop out.\\n/// Called after the ranker has sorted descending by score, so\\n/// the surviving row is the highest-ranked entry per text --\\n/// the buffer-words copy of `outer` outranks the tree-sitter\\n/// copy at the spec's 100/80 priority split, so the popup row\\n/// for `outer` carries the buffer-words tag.\\n///\\n/// Selection / navigation / accept all index into the deduped\\n/// vec naturally; this is the only place we coalesce rows\\n/// across sources, and it runs before the popup paints.\\npub(super) fn dedup_rendered_by_text(rendered: &mut Vec<lattice_completion::RenderedCandidate>) {\\n    let mut seen: std::collections::HashSet<String> = std::collections::HashSet::new();\\n    rendered.retain(|cand| seen.insert(cand.raw.text.clone()));\\n}\\n\\n/// True for bytes the path-completion source treats as part of\\n/// a filename / directory component. Wider than `is_word_char_byte`\\n/// so common filename characters (`.`, `-`, `~`) ride the same\\n/// segment; the trigger anchor breaks at `/` (dir boundary)\\n/// rather than at these characters.\\npub(super) fn is_path_byte(b: u8) -> bool {\\n    b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(b, b'_' | b'-' | b'.' | b'~' | b'+' | b'@')\\n}\\n\\n/// Expand `~/...` against `$HOME` and absolutise a relative\\n/// path against the process's current working directory.\\n///\\n/// Two failure modes this closes:\\n///\\n/// 1. `:e ~/foo.rs` -- without expansion, `Document::open`\\n///    forwards the literal `~` to `read_to_string` and fails\\n///    ENOENT. Cmdline completion (`gen:files`) already does\\n///    its own tilde expansion for `read_dir`, which is why\\n///    completion appears to work but submit fails.\\n///\\n/// 2. Oil opened at a single-component relative path (`src`,\\n///    `foo.rs`, `.`) navigating up. `Path::parent()` returns\\n///    `Some(\\\"\\\")` for those, and `read_dir(\\\"\\\")` is ENOENT.\\n///    Normalising before storing keeps `OilDir` absolute, so\\n///    `parent()` walks the filesystem correctly.\\n///\\n/// We deliberately do not call `canonicalize` -- it requires\\n/// the target to exist (`:e new.rs` against an unsaved path\\n/// has to work) and would surprise users by resolving symlinks\\n/// vim treats as opaque. Cwd-failure or HOME-missing falls\\n/// through to the input verbatim; the caller's open then\\n/// produces the same error it would have produced without\\n/// the normalise step.\\npub(super) fn normalize_user_path(path: &std::path::Path) -> std::path::PathBuf {\\n    let expanded = expand_tilde(path);\\n    if expanded.is_absolute() {\\n        return expanded;\\n    }\\n    match std::env::current_dir() {\\n        Ok(cwd) => cwd.join(expanded),\\n        Err(_) => expanded,\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n/// `~/rest` → `$HOME/rest`, `~` alone → `$HOME`. Anything else\\n/// passes through unchanged. Mirrors the helper in\\n/// `lattice-completion::builtins::generators` -- they stay\\n/// in lockstep because the cmdline-completion source and the\\n/// `:e` submit path both flow through user-typed strings.\\nfn expand_tilde(path: &std::path::Path) -> std::path::PathBuf {\\n    let Some(s) = path.to_str() else {\\n        return path.to_path_buf();\\n    };\\n    let Some(home) = std::env::var_os(\\\"HOME\\\") else {\\n        return path.to_path_buf();\\n    };\\n    if s == \\\"~\\\" {\\n        return std::path::PathBuf::from(home);\\n    }\\n    if let Some(rest) = s.strip_prefix(\\\"~/\\\") {\\n        return std::path::PathBuf::from(home).join(rest);\\n    }\\n    path.to_path_buf()\\n}\\n\\n/// True if `line_idx` is empty or whitespace-only. Used by the\\n/// fold-aware j/k snap to swallow trailing blanks between sibling\\n/// folds (so `j` from a closed fold's heading lands on the next\\n/// sibling's heading, not on the blank between them).\\npub(super) fn is_blank_line(buffer: &lattice_core::Buffer, line_idx: u32) -> bool {\\n    buffer\\n        .line(line_idx)\\n        .map(|s| s.trim().is_empty())\\n        .unwrap_or(true)\\n}\\n\\n/// Phase 4.2 features (hover, definition, references, completion)\\n/// all need this; later we'll thread the per-server negotiated\\n/// `PositionEncodingKind` through here so utf-8 / utf-32 servers\\n/// don't pay the utf-16 conversion. For 4.2.b utf-16 is correct\\n/// for every server we care about today.\\n/// Render an LSP `SignatureHelp` response into a markdown body\\n/// the popup renderer can display. Picks the active signature\\n/// (server-supplied `active_signature` index, default 0) and\\n/// inlines the active parameter's documentation when present.\\n/// Returns the empty string when the response carries no\\n/// signatures.\\npub(crate) fn signature_help_to_markdown(sh: &lsp_types::SignatureHelp) -> String {\\n    if sh.signatures.is_empty() {\\n        return String::new();\\n    }\\n    let active_sig_idx = sh.active_signature.unwrap_or(0) as usize;\\n    let sig = sh\\n        .signatures\\n        .get(active_sig_idx)\\n        .or_else(|| sh.signatures.first())\\n        .expect(\\\"non-empty checked above\\\");\\n    let mut out = String::new();\\n    // Active signature's call form -- renders as a fenced code\\n    // block so the popup's markdown highlighter picks up\\n    // syntax highlighting (whatever language the server says\\n    // -- we don't know, so default to text).\\n    out.push_str(\\\"```text\\\\n\\\");\\n    out.push_str(&sig.label);\\n    out.push_str(\\\"\\\\n```\\\\n\\\");\\n    // Parameter highlight: append a short note pointing at the\\n    // active parameter's name. The popup overlay doesn't yet\\n    // do per-character paragraph styling, so this is the\\n    // friendliest representation we have without bespoke\\n    // rendering.\\n    if let Some(active_param_idx) = sig.active_parameter.or(sh.active_parameter)\\n        && let Some(params) = sig.parameters.as_ref()\\n        && let Some(param) = params.get(active_param_idx as usize)\\n    {\\n        let label_str = match &param.label {\\n            lsp_types::ParameterLabel::Simple(s) => s.clone(),\\n            lsp_types::ParameterLabel::LabelOffsets(_) => String::new(),\\n        };\\n        if !label_str.is_empty() {\\n            out.push_str(&format!(\\\"\\\\n**param:** `{label_str}`\\\\n\\\"));\\n        }\\n        if let Some(doc) = param.documentation.as_ref() {\\n            let doc_str = match doc {\\n                lsp_types::Documentation::String(s) => s.clone(),\\n                lsp_types::Documentation::MarkupContent(mc) => mc.value.clone(),\\n            };\\n            if !doc_str.is_empty() {\\n                out.push('\\\\n');\\n                out.push_str(&doc_str);\\n                out.push('\\\\n');\\n            }\\n        }\\n    }\\n    // Signature-level documentation when present.\\n    if let Some(doc) = sig.documentation.as_ref() {\\n        let doc_str = match doc {\\n            lsp_types::Documentation::String(s) => s.clone(),\\n            lsp_types::Documentation::MarkupContent(mc) => mc.value.clone(),\\n        };\\n        if !doc_str.is_empty() {\\n            out.push('\\\\n');\\n            out.push_str(&doc_str);\\n            out.push('\\\\n');\\n        }\\n    }\\n    out\\n}\\n\\n/// Inverse of `app_to_lsp_position` -- LSP utf-16 character\\n/// column → utf-8 byte column on the given line. Used by\\n/// `apply_lsp_text_edits` to convert TextEdit ranges back to\\n/// the App's `Position` shape.\\npub(crate) fn lsp_position_to_app_byte(buffer: &Buffer, line: u32, character: u32) -> u32 {\\n    let line_text = buffer.line(line).unwrap_or_default();\\n    lattice_lsp::position::utf16_column_to_utf8_byte(&line_text, character)\\n}\\n\\n/// 4.4.e: does the App `(line, byte)` cursor sit inside the\\n/// half-open LSP `range`? We compare only by (line, character)\\n/// in LSP utf-16 space because the range itself is LSP-shape;\\n/// the App cursor is converted on the fly.\\npub(crate) fn cursor_inside_range(cursor: Position, range: &lsp_types::Range) -> bool {\\n    let line = cursor.line;\\n    let col = cursor.byte;\\n    let start = (range.start.line, range.start.character);\\n    let end = (range.end.line, range.end.character);\\n    let here = (line, col);\\n    here >= start && here < end\\n}\\n\\n/// 4.4.f: convert an LSP `FoldingRange` to our `Fold`. LSP\\n/// returns line-based extents; the identity hash combines\\n/// start_line + end_line + kind so closed-state survives\\n/// re-fetches that produce the same logical fold.\\npub(crate) fn folding_range_to_fold(r: lsp_types::FoldingRange) -> Fold {\\n    use std::hash::{Hash, Hasher};\\n    let mut hasher = std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher::new();\\n    r.start_line.hash(&mut hasher);\\n    r.end_line.hash(&mut hasher);\\n    // Spec omits a stable u32 for `kind`; hash the string form\\n    // when present so a fold's kind change still re-keys.\\n    if let Some(kind) = r.kind.as_ref() {\\n        std::mem::discriminant(kind).hash(&mut hasher);\\n    }\\n    Fold {\\n        start_line: r.start_line,\\n        end_line: r.end_line,\\n        closed: false,\\n        identity: Some(hasher.finish()),\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n/// 4.4.e: flatten an LSP `SelectionRange` (linked list via\\n/// `parent`) into a `Vec<Range>` ordered innermost-first.\\npub(crate) fn flatten_selection_range_chain(\\n    head: &lsp_types::SelectionRange,\\n) -> Vec<lsp_types::Range> {\\n    let mut out = Vec::new();\\n    let mut cur = Some(head);\\n    while let Some(node) = cur {\\n        out.push(node.range);\\n        cur = node.parent.as_deref();\\n    }\\n    out\\n}\\n\\npub(crate) fn app_to_lsp_position(buffer: &Buffer, p: Position) -> Option<lsp_types::Position> {\\n    let line_text = buffer.line(p.line)?;\\n    let character = lattice_lsp::position::utf8_byte_to_utf16_column(&line_text, p.byte);\\n    Some(lsp_types::Position {\\n        line: p.line,\\n        character,\\n    })\\n}\\n\\n/// Flatten a `DocumentSymbolResponse` into our pre-rendered\\n/// `SymbolRow` shape. The legacy `Flat(Vec<SymbolInformation>)`\\n/// variant is one row per symbol with no nesting; the modern\\n/// `Nested(Vec<DocumentSymbol>)` variant carries\\n/// `children: Vec<DocumentSymbol>`, walked depth-first to\\n/// preserve outline ordering.\\npub(crate) fn flatten_document_symbol_response(\\n    resp: lsp_types::DocumentSymbolResponse,\\n    path: &std::path::Path,\\n    out: &mut Vec<SymbolRow>,\\n) {\\n    match resp {\\n        lsp_types::DocumentSymbolResponse::Flat(syms) => {\\n            for sym in syms {\\n                if let Some(row) = symbol_information_to_row(&sym) {\\n                    out.push(row);\\n                }\\n            }\\n        }\\n        lsp_types::DocumentSymbolResponse::Nested(syms) => {\\n            fn walk(\\n                syms: Vec<lsp_types::DocumentSymbol>,\\n                path: &std::path::Path,\\n                depth: u32,\\n                out: &mut Vec<SymbolRow>,\\n            ) {\\n                for sym in syms {\\n                    out.push(SymbolRow {\\n                        name: sym.name.clone(),\\n                        kind_glyph: symbol_kind_glyph(sym.kind),\\n                        container: None,\\n                        depth,\\n                        path: path.to_path_buf(),\\n                        line: sym.selection_range.start.line,\\n                        col: sym.selection_range.start.character,\\n                    });\\n                    if let Some(children) = sym.children {\\n                        walk(children, path, depth + 1, out);\\n                    }\\n                }\\n            }\\n            walk(syms, path, 0, out);\\n        }\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n/// Map a flat `SymbolInformation` (legacy outline + workspace\\n/// symbol shape) into our row type. Returns `None` when the\\n/// location's URI doesn't resolve to a path.\\n/// Convert a modern (LSP 3.17+) `WorkspaceSymbol` into a\\n/// `SymbolRow` (Phase 4.2 follow-up). When the symbol's\\n/// `location` came back as the `WorkspaceLocation` (URI-only)\\n/// variant, fires `workspaceSymbol/resolve` against the\\n/// originating server to upgrade to a real `Location` with\\n/// `range`. Returns `None` when:\\n/// - The URI doesn't map to a path.\\n/// - Resolve fails (server doesn't actually advertise it,\\n///   or returns a still-unresolved shape).\\n/// - Cancellation fires while we're awaiting resolve.\\npub(crate) async fn workspace_symbol_to_row(\\n    handle: &lattice_lsp::ServerHandle,\\n    sym: lsp_types::WorkspaceSymbol,\\n    token: &lattice_protocol::CancellationToken,\\n) -> Option<SymbolRow> {\\n    use lsp_types::OneOf;\\n    let (path, line, col) = match &sym.location {\\n        OneOf::Left(loc) => (\\n            lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&loc.uri)?,\\n            loc.range.start.line,\\n            loc.range.start.character,\\n        ),\\n        OneOf::Right(wsl) => {\\n            let path = lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&wsl.uri)?;\\n            // Server's resolveProvider absent -> no point firing.\\n            // Fall back to (0, 0); the user can still navigate\\n            // to the file.\\n            if !handle.capabilities().workspace_symbol_resolve_provider() {\\n                (path, 0, 0)\\n            } else {\\n                match handle\\n                    .workspace_symbol_resolve(sym.clone(), token.clone())\\n                    .await\\n                {\\n                    Ok(resolved) => match resolved.location {\\n                        OneOf::Left(loc) => (\\n                            lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&loc.uri).unwrap_or(path),\\n                            loc.range.start.line,\\n                            loc.range.start.character,\\n                        ),\\n                        // Server replied without populating range\\n                        // -- spec violation, but defensive: fall\\n                        // back to (0, 0) instead of dropping.\\n                        OneOf::Right(_) => (path, 0, 0),\\n                    },\\n                    // Resolve failed -- log via the symbol's\\n                    // path-only fallback. Caller still gets a\\n                    // navigable row.\\n                    Err(_) => (path, 0, 0),\\n                }\\n            }\\n        }\\n    };\\n    Some(SymbolRow {\\n        name: sym.name,\\n        kind_glyph: symbol_kind_glyph(sym.kind),\\n        container: sym.container_name,\\n        depth: 0,\\n        path,\\n        line,\\n        col,\\n    })\\n}\\n\\npub(crate) fn symbol_information_to_row(sym: &lsp_types::SymbolInformation) -> Option<SymbolRow> {\\n    let path = lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&sym.location.uri)?;\\n    Some(SymbolRow {\\n        name: sym.name.clone(),\\n        kind_glyph: symbol_kind_glyph(sym.kind),\\n        container: sym.container_name.clone(),\\n        depth: 0,\\n        path,\\n        line: sym.location.range.start.line,\\n        col: sym.location.range.start.character,\\n    })\\n}\\n\\n/// 4.5.a: render one `CallHierarchyItem` (the caller in an\\n/// `IncomingCall.from` or the callee in an\\n/// `OutgoingCall.to`) as a [`SymbolRow`] for the picker. The\\n/// item's `detail` (if any) plus the *originating* callable's\\n/// name ride in `container` -- e.g. for an incoming-calls\\n/// listing of `foo`, the rows say \\\"bar.rs:42 fn quux  (in foo)\\\".\\n/// Falls back to `(path, 0, 0)` if the URI doesn't parse;\\n/// keeping the row visible beats silently dropping it.\\npub(crate) fn call_hierarchy_to_row(\\n    item: &lsp_types::CallHierarchyItem,\\n    related_to: &str,\\n) -> SymbolRow {\\n    let path = lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&item.uri).unwrap_or_default();\\n    SymbolRow {\\n        name: item.name.clone(),\\n        kind_glyph: symbol_kind_glyph(item.kind),\\n        container: Some(format!(\\\"in {related_to}\\\")),\\n        depth: 0,\\n        path,\\n        line: item.selection_range.start.line,\\n        col: item.selection_range.start.character,\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n/// 4.5.c: does the given `range` cover the LSP `position`?\\n/// Inclusive on both ends (matches VSCode's \\\"click-through\\\"\\n/// semantics on a link's rightmost char). Used by the `gx`\\n/// keystroke to find the first cached `documentLink` under\\n/// the cursor.\\npub(crate) fn range_covers(range: lsp_types::Range, position: lsp_types::Position) -> bool {\\n    let after_start =\\n        (range.start.line, range.start.character) <= (position.line, position.character);\\n    let before_end = (position.line, position.character) <= (range.end.line, range.end.character);\\n    after_start && before_end\\n}\\n\\n/// 4.5.b: render one `TypeHierarchyItem` (a supertype or\\n/// subtype of the cursor's type) as a [`SymbolRow`] for the\\n/// picker. Same projection as [`call_hierarchy_to_row`]\\n/// because the item shape is identical (name, kind, uri,\\n/// range, selection_range); the container hint differs\\n/// (`\\\"super of foo\\\"` / `\\\"sub of foo\\\"`).\\npub(crate) fn type_hierarchy_to_row(\\n    item: &lsp_types::TypeHierarchyItem,\\n    related_to: &str,\\n) -> SymbolRow {\\n    let path = lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&item.uri).unwrap_or_default();\\n    SymbolRow {\\n        name: item.name.clone(),\\n        kind_glyph: symbol_kind_glyph(item.kind),\\n        container: Some(format!(\\\"of {related_to}\\\")),\\n        depth: 0,\\n        path,\\n        line: item.selection_range.start.line,\\n        col: item.selection_range.start.character,\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n/// Extract a placeholder string from a `PrepareRenameResponse`.\\n/// The spec gives three shapes: a Range (no placeholder, just\\n/// \\\"you can rename here\\\"), a Range+Placeholder (preferred), or\\n/// a DefaultBehavior signal (server defers to the editor's\\n/// word-under-cursor heuristic). We pull the placeholder when\\n/// present, else `None` so the App's caller can fall back to\\n/// the heuristic.\\npub(crate) fn prepare_rename_placeholder(\\n    resp: &lsp_types::PrepareRenameResponse,\\n) -> Option<String> {\\n    match resp {\\n        lsp_types::PrepareRenameResponse::RangeWithPlaceholder { placeholder, .. } => {\\n            Some(placeholder.clone())\\n        }\\n        lsp_types::PrepareRenameResponse::Range(_) => None,\\n        lsp_types::PrepareRenameResponse::DefaultBehavior { .. } => None,\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n/// Flatten a `WorkspaceEdit` into a per-file\\n/// `Vec<(Uri, Vec<TextEdit>)>`. Handles both the legacy `changes`\\n/// HashMap shape and the modern `document_changes` shape (which\\n/// also carries DocumentChangeOperation::Op create/rename/delete\\n/// -- those are skipped in v1; rename returns plain text edits\\n/// for ~100% of identifiers).\\n///\\n/// Empty Vec means \\\"nothing to apply\\\" (the App echoes `Empty`).\\npub(crate) fn flatten_workspace_edit(\\n    we: lsp_types::WorkspaceEdit,\\n) -> Vec<(lsp_types::Uri, Vec<lsp_types::TextEdit>)> {\\n    let mut out: Vec<(lsp_types::Uri, Vec<lsp_types::TextEdit>)> = Vec::new();\\n    if let Some(changes) = we.changes {\\n        for (uri, edits) in changes {\\n            if !edits.is_empty() {\\n                out.push((uri, edits));\\n            }\\n        }\\n    }\\n    if let Some(doc_changes) = we.document_changes {\\n        match doc_changes {\\n            lsp_types::DocumentChanges::Edits(edits) => {\\n                for te_doc in edits {\\n                    let uri = te_doc.text_document.uri.clone();\\n                    let raw_edits: Vec<lsp_types::TextEdit> = te_doc\\n                        .edits\\n                        .into_iter()\\n                        .filter_map(|e| match e {\\n                            lsp_types::OneOf::Left(te) => Some(te),\\n                            // AnnotatedTextEdit -- strip the\\n                            // annotation; v1 doesn't surface\\n                            // change-annotations to the user.\\n                            lsp_types::OneOf::Right(ate) => Some(ate.text_edit),\\n                        })\\n                        .collect();\\n                    if !raw_edits.is_empty() {\\n                        out.push((uri, raw_edits));\\n                    }\\n                }\\n            }\\n            // create-file / rename-file / delete-file ops are\\n            // skipped in v1 -- the rename use case is identifier\\n            // rewrites, which servers return as plain text edits.\\n            lsp_types::DocumentChanges::Operations(_) => {}\\n        }\\n    }\\n    out\\n}\\n\\n/// Single-character glyph for an LSP `CodeActionKind`. Maps\\n/// the standard kinds (quickfix, refactor*, source*) to a\\n/// short visual marker for the picker margin. Unknown / custom\\n/// kinds and bare `Command` payloads land on `?`.\\npub(crate) fn code_action_kind_glyph(kind: Option<&lsp_types::CodeActionKind>) -> &'static str {\\n    use lsp_types::CodeActionKind as K;\\n    let Some(kind) = kind else {\\n        return \\\"?\\\";\\n    };\\n    if *kind == K::QUICKFIX {\\n        \\\"🛠\\\"\\n    } else if *kind == K::REFACTOR {\\n        \\\"♻\\\"\\n    } else if *kind == K::REFACTOR_EXTRACT {\\n        \\\"↗\\\"\\n    } else if *kind == K::REFACTOR_INLINE {\\n        \\\"↘\\\"\\n    } else if *kind == K::REFACTOR_REWRITE {\\n        \\\"↺\\\"\\n    } else if *kind == K::SOURCE {\\n        \\\"★\\\"\\n    } else if *kind == K::SOURCE_ORGANIZE_IMPORTS {\\n        \\\"≡\\\"\\n    } else if *kind == K::SOURCE_FIX_ALL {\\n        \\\"✓\\\"\\n    } else {\\n        \\\"?\\\"\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n/// Single-character glyph for an LSP `CompletionItemKind`.\\n/// Same shape as `symbol_kind_glyph` but maps the completion-\\n/// item kind enum (which is wider -- snippets, keywords,\\n/// folders, etc.). The `*messages*` buffer's per-tick drain\\n    ///    ([`Self::drain_message_events`]) appends each record.\\n    ///\\n    /// **msg-mode.1 contract:** `set_message` writes directly\\n    /// to the ring + bus (the legacy path). The\\n    /// [`lattice_runtime::MessagesLayer`] installed at boot\\n    /// captures every *other* `tracing::*` event in the editor\\n    /// (LSP layer logs, plugin host, future telemetry) into\\n    /// the same ring + bus. Keeping\\n    /// `set_message` independent of the global subscriber\\n    /// preserves per-App isolation — each App's bus + ring are\\n    /// the only consumers of its own `set_message` calls.\\n    pub fn set_message(&mut self, level: EchoLevel, text: impl Into<String>) {\\n        let text: String = text.into();\\n        self.editor.last_message = Some(EchoMessage {\\n            text: text.clone(),\\n            level,\\n        });\\n        let record = MessageRecord {\\n            timestamp: std::time::SystemTime::now(),\\n            level: echo_level_to_wire(level),\\n            text,\\n        };\\n        if let Ok(mut ring) = self.editor.messages.lock() {\\n            ring.push(record.clone());\\n        }\\n        self.editor.event_bus.publish_typed(MessagePushed { record });\\n    }\\n}\\n\\npub(crate) fn line_byte_len(buf: &Buffer, line: u32) -> u32 {\\n    // §8.2 hot path: use ropey's O(log n) line API instead of\\n    // materialising the whole buffer.\\n    buf.line_byte_len(line)\\n}\\n\\npub(crate) fn last_addressable_line(buf: &Buffer) -> u32 {\\n    let lc = buf.line_count();\\n    if lc == 0 {\\n        return 0;\\n    }\\n    // ropey reports an extra empty line for any rope ending in\\n    // `\\\\n`. Detect that by checking whether the last \\\"line\\\" the\\n    // rope reports is empty, without materialising the entire\\n    // buffer text.\\n    let last_idx = lc - 1;\\n    if buf.line_byte_len(last_idx) == 0 && lc >= 2 {\\n        last_idx - 1\\n    } else {\\n        last_idx\\n    }\\n}\\n\\npub(super) fn is_valid_mark_name(c: char) -> bool {\\n    c.is_ascii_alphabetic() || c.is_ascii_digit()\\n}\\n\\n/// Render a register's content into a one-line preview (truncated and\\n/// with newlines escaped). Used by `:reg`.\\npub(super) fn preview_register(s: &str) -> String {\\n    const MAX: usize = 40;\\n    let escaped: String = s\\n        .chars()\\n        .map(|c| if c == '\\\\n' { '\\\\u{21B5}' } else { c })\\n        .collect();\\n    if escaped.chars().count() <= MAX {\\n        escaped\\n    } else {\\n        let trimmed: String = escaped.chars().take(MAX).collect();\\n        format!(\\\"{trimmed}…\\\")\\n    }\\n}\\n\\npub(super) fn is_word_char_byte(b: u8) -> bool {\\n    b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b == b'_'\\n}\\n\\n/// Cross-source visual dedup for the insert-completion popup\\n/// (Phase 4.2.g.7 polish). Keeps the FIRST occurrence of each\\n/// `raw.text`; subsequent rows with the same text drop out.\\n/// Called after the ranker has sorted descending by score, so\\n/// the surviving row is the highest-ranked entry per text --\\n/// the buffer-words copy of `outer` outranks the tree-sitter\\n/// copy at the spec's 100/80 priority split, so the popup row\\n/// for `outer` carries the buffer-words tag.\\n///\\n/// Selection / navigation / accept all index into the deduped\\n/// vec naturally; this is the only place we coalesce rows\\n/// across sources, and it runs before the popup paints.\\npub(super) fn dedup_rendered_by_text(rendered: &mut Vec<lattice_completion::RenderedCandidate>) {\\n    let mut seen: std::collections::HashSet<String> = std::collections::HashSet::new();\\n    rendered.retain(|cand| seen.insert(cand.raw.text.clone()));\\n}\\n\\n/// True for bytes the path-completion source treats as part of\\n/// a filename / directory component. Wider than `is_word_char_byte`\\n/// so common filename characters (`.`, `-`, `~`) ride the same\\n/// segment; the trigger anchor breaks at `/` (dir boundary)\\n/// rather than at these characters.\\npub(super) fn is_path_byte(b: u8) -> bool {\\n    b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(b, b'_' | b'-' | b'.' | b'~' | b'+' | b'@')\\n}\\n\\n/// Expand `~/...` against `$HOME` and absolutise a relative\\n/// path against the process's current working directory.\\n///\\n/// Two failure modes this closes:\\n///\\n/// 1. `:e ~/foo.rs` -- without expansion, `Document::open`\\n///    forwards the literal `~` to `read_to_string` and fails\\n///    ENOENT. Cwd-failure or HOME-missing falls\\n/// through to the input verbatim; the caller's open then\\n/// produces the same error it would have produced without\\n/// the normalise step.\\npub(super) fn normalize_user_path(path: &std::path::Path) -> std::path::PathBuf {\\n    let expanded = expand_tilde(path);\\n    if expanded.is_absolute() {\\n        return expanded;\\n    }\\n    match std::env::current_dir() {\\n        Ok(cwd) => cwd.join(expanded),\\n        Err(_) => expanded,\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n/// `~/rest` → `$HOME/rest`, `~` alone → `$HOME`. Mirrors the helper in\\n/// `lattice-completion::builtins::generators` -- they stay\\n/// in lockstep because the cmdline-completion source and the\\n/// `:e` submit path both flow through user-typed strings.\\nfn expand_tilde(path: &std::path::Path) -> std::path::PathBuf {\\n    let Some(s) = path.to_str() else {\\n        return path.to_path_buf();\\n    };\\n    let Some(home) = std::env::var_os(\\\"HOME\\\") else {\\n        return path.to_path_buf();\\n    };\\n    if s == \\\"~\\\" {\\n        return std::path::PathBuf::from(home);\\n    }\\n    if let Some(rest) = s.strip_prefix(\\\"~/\\\") {\\n        return std::path::PathBuf::from(home).join(rest);\\n    }\\n    path.to_path_buf()\\n}\\n\\n/// True if `line_idx` is empty or whitespace-only. Used by the\\n/// fold-aware j/k snap to swallow trailing blanks between sibling\\n/// folds (so `j` from a closed fold's heading lands on the next\\n/// sibling's heading, not on the blank between them).\\npub(super) fn is_blank_line(buffer: &lattice_core::Buffer, line_idx: u32) -> bool {\\n    buffer\\n        .line(line_idx)\\n        .map(|s| s.trim().is_empty())\\n        .unwrap_or(true)\\n}\\n\\n/// Phase 4.2 features (hover, definition, references, completion)\\n/// all need this; later we'll thread the per-server negotiated\\n/// `PositionEncodingKind` through here so utf-8 / utf-32 servers\\n/// don't pay the utf-16 conversion. For 4.2.b utf-16 is correct\\n/// for every server we care about today.\\n/// Render an LSP `SignatureHelp` response into a markdown body\\n/// the popup renderer can display. Picks the active signature\\n/// (server-supplied `active_signature` index, default 0) and\\n/// inlines the active parameter's documentation when present.\\n/// Returns the empty string when the response carries no\\n/// signatures.\\npub(crate) fn signature_help_to_markdown(sh: &lsp_types::SignatureHelp) -> String {\\n    if sh.signatures.is_empty() {\\n        return String::new();\\n    }\\n    let active_sig_idx = sh.active_signature.unwrap_or(0) as usize;\\n    let sig = sh\\n        .signatures\\n        .get(active_sig_idx)\\n        .or_else(|| sh.signatures.first())\\n        .expect(\\\"non-empty checked above\\\");\\n    let mut out = String::new();\\n    // Active signature's call form -- renders as a fenced code\\n    // block so the popup's markdown highlighter picks up\\n    // syntax highlighting (whatever language the server says\\n    // -- we don't know, so default to text).\\n    out.push_str(\\\"```text\\\\n\\\");\\n    out.push_str(&sig.label);\\n    out.push_str(\\\"\\\\n```\\\\n\\\");\\n    // Parameter highlight: append a short note pointing at the\\n    // active parameter's name. The popup overlay doesn't yet\\n    // do per-character paragraph styling, so this is the\\n    // friendliest representation we have without bespoke\\n    // rendering.\\n    if let Some(active_param_idx) = sig.active_parameter.or(sh.active_parameter)\\n        && let Some(params) = sig.parameters.as_ref()\\n        && let Some(param) = params.get(active_param_idx as usize)\\n    {\\n        let label_str = match &param.label {\\n            lsp_types::ParameterLabel::Simple(s) => s.clone(),\\n            lsp_types::ParameterLabel::LabelOffsets(_) => String::new(),\\n        };\\n        if !label_str.is_empty() {\\n            out.push_str(&format!(\\\"\\\\n**param:** `{label_str}`\\\\n\\\"));\\n        }\\n        if let Some(doc) = param.documentation.as_ref() {\\n            let doc_str = match doc {\\n                lsp_types::Documentation::String(s) => s.clone(),\\n                lsp_types::Documentation::MarkupContent(mc) => mc.value.clone(),\\n            };\\n            if !doc_str.is_empty() {\\n                out.push('\\\\n');\\n                out.push_str(&doc_str);\\n                out.push('\\\\n');\\n            }\\n        }\\n    }\\n    // Signature-level documentation when present.\\n    if let Some(doc) = sig.documentation.as_ref() {\\n        let doc_str = match doc {\\n            lsp_types::Documentation::String(s) => s.clone(),\\n            lsp_types::Documentation::MarkupContent(mc) => mc.value.clone(),\\n        };\\n        if !doc_str.is_empty() {\\n            out.push('\\\\n');\\n            out.push_str(&doc_str);\\n            out.push('\\\\n');\\n        }\\n    }\\n    out\\n}\\n\\n/// Inverse of `app_to_lsp_position` -- LSP utf-16 character\\n/// column → utf-8 byte column on the given line. Used by\\n/// `apply_lsp_text_edits` to convert TextEdit ranges back to\\n/// the App's `Position` shape.\\npub(crate) fn lsp_position_to_app_byte(buffer: &Buffer, line: u32, character: u32) -> u32 {\\n    let line_text = buffer.line(line).unwrap_or_default();\\n    lattice_lsp::position::utf16_column_to_utf8_byte(&line_text, character)\\n}\\n\\n/// 4.4.e: does the App `(line, byte)` cursor sit inside the\\n/// half-open LSP `range`? We compare only by (line, character)\\n/// in LSP utf-16 space because the range itself is LSP-shape;\\n/// the App cursor is converted on the fly.\\npub(crate) fn cursor_inside_range(cursor: Position, range: &lsp_types::Range) -> bool {\\n    let line = cursor.line;\\n    let col = cursor.byte;\\n    let start = (range.start.line, range.start.character);\\n    let end = (range.end.line, range.end.character);\\n    let here = (line, col);\\n    here >= start && here < end\\n}\\n\\n/// 4.4.f: convert an LSP `FoldingRange` to our `Fold`. LSP\\n/// returns line-based extents; the identity hash combines\\n/// start_line + end_line + kind so closed-state survives\\n/// re-fetches that produce the same logical fold.\\npub(crate) fn folding_range_to_fold(r: lsp_types::FoldingRange) -> Fold {\\n    use std::hash::{Hash, Hasher};\\n    let mut hasher = std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher::new();\\n    r.start_line.hash(&mut hasher);\\n    r.end_line.hash(&mut hasher);\\n    // Spec omits a stable u32 for `kind`; hash the string form\\n    // when present so a fold's kind change still re-keys.\\n    if let Some(kind) = r.kind.as_ref() {\\n        std::mem::discriminant(kind).hash(&mut hasher);\\n    }\\n    Fold {\\n        start_line: r.start_line,\\n        end_line: r.end_line,\\n        closed: false,\\n        identity: Some(hasher.finish()),\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n/// 4.4.e: flatten an LSP `SelectionRange` (linked list via\\n/// `parent`) into a `Vec<Range>` ordered innermost-first.\\npub(crate) fn flatten_selection_range_chain(\\n    head: &lsp_types::SelectionRange,\\n) -> Vec<lsp_types::Range> {\\n    let mut out = Vec::new();\\n    let mut cur = Some(head);\\n    while let Some(node) = cur {\\n        out.push(node.range);\\n        cur = node.parent.as_deref();\\n    }\\n    out\\n}\\n\\npub(crate) fn app_to_lsp_position(buffer: &Buffer, p: Position) -> Option<lsp_types::Position> {\\n    let line_text = buffer.line(p.line)?;\\n    let character = lattice_lsp::position::utf8_byte_to_utf16_column(&line_text, p.byte);\\n    Some(lsp_types::Position {\\n        line: p.line,\\n        character,\\n    })\\n}\\n\\n/// Flatten a `DocumentSymbolResponse` into our pre-rendered\\n/// `SymbolRow` shape. The legacy `Flat(Vec<SymbolInformation>)`\\n/// variant is one row per symbol with no nesting; the modern\\n/// `Nested(Vec<DocumentSymbol>)` variant carries\\n/// `children: Vec<DocumentSymbol>`, walked depth-first to\\n/// preserve outline ordering.\\npub(crate) fn flatten_document_symbol_response(\\n    resp: lsp_types::DocumentSymbolResponse,\\n    path: &std::path::Path,\\n    out: &mut Vec<SymbolRow>,\\n) {\\n    match resp {\\n        lsp_types::DocumentSymbolResponse::Flat(syms) => {\\n            for sym in syms {\\n                if let Some(row) = symbol_information_to_row(&sym) {\\n                    out.push(row);\\n                }\\n            }\\n        }\\n        lsp_types::DocumentSymbolResponse::Nested(syms) => {\\n            fn walk(\\n                syms: Vec<lsp_types::DocumentSymbol>,\\n                path: &std::path::Path,\\n                depth: u32,\\n                out: &mut Vec<SymbolRow>,\\n            ) {\\n                for sym in syms {\\n                    out.push(SymbolRow {\\n                        name: sym.name.clone(),\\n                        kind_glyph: symbol_kind_glyph(sym.kind),\\n                        container: None,\\n                        depth,\\n                        path: path.to_path_buf(),\\n                        line: sym.selection_range.start.line,\\n                        col: sym.selection_range.start.character,\\n                    });\\n                    if let Some(children) = sym.children {\\n                        walk(children, path, depth + 1, out);\\n                    }\\n                }\\n            }\\n            walk(syms, path, 0, out);\\n        }\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n/// Map a flat `SymbolInformation` (legacy outline + workspace\\n/// symbol shape) into our row type. Returns `None` when the\\n/// location's URI doesn't resolve to a path.\\n/// Convert a modern (LSP 3.17+) `WorkspaceSymbol` into a\\n/// `SymbolRow` (Phase 4.2 follow-up). Returns `None` when:\\n/// - The URI doesn't map to a path.\\n/// - Resolve fails (server doesn't actually advertise it,\\n///   or returns a still-unresolved shape).\\n/// - Cancellation fires while we're awaiting resolve.\\npub(crate) async fn workspace_symbol_to_row(\\n    handle: &lattice_lsp::ServerHandle,\\n    sym: lsp_types::WorkspaceSymbol,\\n    token: &lattice_protocol::CancellationToken,\\n) -> Option<SymbolRow> {\\n    use lsp_types::OneOf;\\n    let (path, line, col) = match &sym.location {\\n        OneOf::Left(loc) => (\\n            lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&loc.uri)?,\\n            loc.range.start.line,\\n            loc.range.start.character,\\n        ),\\n        OneOf::Right(wsl) => {\\n            let path = lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&wsl.uri)?;\\n            // Server's resolveProvider absent -> no point firing.\\n            // Fall back to (0, 0); the user can still navigate\\n            // to the file.\\n            if !handle.capabilities().workspace_symbol_resolve_provider() {\\n                (path, 0, 0)\\n            } else {\\n                match handle\\n                    .workspace_symbol_resolve(sym.clone(), token.clone())\\n                    .await\\n                {\\n                    Ok(resolved) => match resolved.location {\\n                        OneOf::Left(loc) => (\\n                            lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&loc.uri).unwrap_or(path),\\n                            loc.range.start.line,\\n                            loc.range.start.character,\\n                        ),\\n                        // Server replied without populating range\\n                        // -- spec violation, but defensive: fall\\n                        // back to (0, 0) instead of dropping.\\n                        OneOf::Right(_) => (path, 0, 0),\\n                    },\\n                    // Resolve failed -- log via the symbol's\\n                    // path-only fallback. Caller still gets a\\n                    // navigable row.\\n                    Err(_) => (path, 0, 0),\\n                }\\n            }\\n        }\\n    };\\n    Some(SymbolRow {\\n        name: sym.name,\\n        kind_glyph: symbol_kind_glyph(sym.kind),\\n        container: sym.container_name,\\n        depth: 0,\\n        path,\\n        line,\\n        col,\\n    })\\n}\\n\\npub(crate) fn symbol_information_to_row(sym: &lsp_types::SymbolInformation) -> Option<SymbolRow> {\\n    let path = lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&sym.location.uri)?;\\n    Some(SymbolRow {\\n        name: sym.name.clone(),\\n        kind_glyph: symbol_kind_glyph(sym.kind),\\n        container: sym.container_name.clone(),\\n        depth: 0,\\n        path,\\n        line: sym.location.range.start.line,\\n        col: sym.location.range.start.character,\\n    })\\n}\\n\\n/// 4.5.a: render one `CallHierarchyItem` (the caller in an\\n/// `IncomingCall.from` or the callee in an\\n/// `OutgoingCall.to`) as a [`SymbolRow`] for the picker. The\\n/// item's `detail` (if any) plus the *originating* callable's\\n/// name ride in `container` -- e.g. for an incoming-calls\\n/// listing of `foo`, the rows say \\\"bar.rs:42 fn quux  (in foo)\\\".\\n/// Falls back to `(path, 0, 0)` if the URI doesn't parse;\\n/// keeping the row visible beats silently dropping it.\\npub(crate) fn call_hierarchy_to_row(\\n    item: &lsp_types::CallHierarchyItem,\\n    related_to: &str,\\n) -> SymbolRow {\\n    let path = lattice_lsp::actor::uri_to_path(&item.uri).unwrap_or_default();\\n    SymbolRow {\\n        name: item.name.clone(),\\n        kind_glyph: symbol_kind_glyph(item.kind),\\n        container: Some(format!(\\\"in {related_to}\\\")),\\n        depth: 0,\\n        path,\\n        line: item.selection_range.start.line,\\n        col: item.selection_range.start.character,\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n/// 4.5.c: does the given `range` cover the LSP `position`?\\n/// Inclusive on both ends (matches VSCode's \\\"click-through\\\"\\n/// semantics on a link's rightmost char).
